title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (reconstructed from pp. 25–27). There is a set 𝓜 of 'models' with a relation X ≪ Y, which I read as 'X lies in the shadow (Omb) of Y'. There are also 'figures' F ∈ 𝓕, each with an underlying set F̃ ⊂ 𝓜. On F̃ the order ≤ is the restriction of ≪. Omb(Y) = {X : X ≪ Y}, and Omb(F) = ⋃_{X∈F̃} Omb(X). The previous page introduces a retraction φ_F : Omb(F) → F̃, sending Y to the smallest X ∈ F̃ with Y ≪ X; it is the identity on F̃. φ_F defines the preorder on |Multiomb F|. It is then asserted that Multiomb(G) ≪ Multiomb(F) means two things: Omb G ⊂ Omb F, and there is an increasing map f : G̃ → F̃ with φ_F|_{Omb G} = f ∘ φ_G (the square labelled (1.48) on p. 25 but cited here as (1.42)).

This page begins the proof that this is equivalent to G ≪ F, i.e. every X ∈ G̃ is ≪ some element of F̃ (condition (C4) on p. 27).

(⇐ part, construction) Assume G ≪ F. Define f(X) = min{Z ∈ F̃ : X ≪ Z}. Then f is increasing: X' ≤ X means X' ≪ X ≪ f(X), so X' ≪ f(X) by transitivity of ≪. By minimality, f(X') ≤ f(X).

What remains is commutativity of the square, φ_F(Y) = f(φ_G(Y)) for Y ∈ Omb G. Grothendieck isolates this as a 'Corollaire': if X ≪ G ≪ F, X' = min G^X and X'' = min F^{X'}, then X'' = min F^X. Here G^X denotes the elements of G̃ dominating X. This is exactly the statement that the nearest-point retractions compose.

He realises this does not follow from the axioms so far. He says it must be posed as an axiom, in a form that looks different but is equivalent. To state it he introduces a new notation, X ∘≪ Y ('X is infinitely interior to Y'), defined by X ∈ Omb(Y)° = Omb(Y) ∖ ⋃_{Y'<Y} Omb(Y'). Equivalently: X ≪ Y, and X ≪ Y' ≤ Y forces Y' = Y. So Y is a minimal dominator of X.

The next page states axiom AE7: ∘≪ is transitive. This yields the commutation, hence the ⇐ direction. The converse is easy: φ_F(X) = f(X) exists for every X ∈ G̃, which gives G ≪ F; monotonicity of f is not needed.

In modern terms: these are posets with 'nearest-point' reflections onto finite subposets. The new axiom says that 'minimal dominator' is a transitive relation, i.e. reflections compose. This is the familiar condition that a reflective subcategory of a reflective subcategory is reflective in the whole, here in a combinatorial/order-theoretic guise. The page is part of an axiomatic, combinatorial foundation for 'analysis situs' (tame topology), building figures as unions of shadows.
errors: Equation-number clash: the commutative square is labelled (1.48) on p. 25 but cited as (1.42) here, and the new notation X ∘≪ Y is also labelled (1.48).
The proof of the equivalence is left incomplete on this page. Commutation of the square is not derived; it is deferred to a new axiom (AE7).

The claimed equivalence between the Corollaire (stated relative to the finite sets G̃, F̃) and transitivity of ∘≪ (stated globally in 𝓜) is asserted, not proved. Minimality inside G̃ need not coincide with minimality among all Y' ≤ Y in 𝓜 unless figures are suitably saturated. So 'en fait équivalent' hides a gap, or relies on unstated properties of figures.
Existence of the minima min G^X and min F^X is used tacitly. It presumably comes from earlier axioms on figures, which I cannot see.

ideas.what: Nearest-point retraction φ_F : Omb(F) → F̃ and characterisation of maps of multishadow figures by a commuting square with an increasing map f
ideas.modern_name: Reflection / closure-type retraction onto a subposet; morphism of posets compatible with reflections (Galois-connection-like)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard order theory / category theory (reflective subcategories)
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Analysis situs drafts (cote 156), as far as I know

ideas.what: Monotonicity of f(X) = min{Z ∈ F̃ : X ≪ Z} via transitivity of ≪
Relation X ∘≪ Y ('infinitely interior'): Y is a minimal element dominating X; axiom AE7 that this relation is transitive, equivalent to composability of the retractions
ideas.modern_name: Transitivity of minimal-cover / minimal-dominator relation; composability of reflections (closest analogue: interpolation-type axioms for way-below relations in domain theory, though different)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard attribution in this form

missed.claim: This page is part of Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 axiomatic foundation for 'analysis situs' (tame topology), built from a 'shadow' relation ≪, figures, Omb and Multiomb. It records the precise point where a new axiom (AE7, transitivity of 'infinitely interior') turns out to be needed so that the retractions onto figures compose. The axiom system itself does not appear in the literature on tame topology or o-minimality.
missed.quote: Il semble qu'il faille la poser [en axiome] ... mais en fait équivalent. On va introduire avant une notation ... X ∘≪ Y (X est infiniment intérieur de Y)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest for reconstructing Grothendieck's tame-topology programme announced in the Esquisse. The page itself contains only routine order-theoretic content.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is elementary order theory: a monotone map built from minimal dominators, plus an extra axiom guaranteeing that retractions compose. Its only interest is as an unpublished step in Grothendieck's axiomatic analysis situs; nothing here would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'Il semble qu'il faille la prouver ici à nouveau, sous forme d'un nouvel postulat' should read approximately 'Il semble qu'il faille la poser [comme/en axiome], sous forme un peu [différente/affaiblie], mais en fait équivalente'. The next page's 'On doit donc poser AE 7' supports 'poser'.
'[-implique-]' is a crossed-out 'implique que', replaced by the insertion '(≪ f(X))'.
Write 𝓜 rather than M for the model set, consistent with neighbouring pages.
The struck line after 'pour' reads '~~X ≪ Y, et X ≪ Y~~'.
